name: Localhost and LAN port scanning
plain: A page probes ports on the visitor's own machine or home network to find running software.
meaning: JavaScript uses fetch, WebSocket or image timing to test localhost ports (eBay's 2020 check, Meta Pixel and Yandex on Android in 2025 messaging via localhost). Chrome LNA prompts since 142 and PNA aim to stop this.

web.api: fetch/WebSocket/img to 127.0.0.1 and RFC1918 hosts; timing

limits.headline: Can try to find software running on your own computer, though Chrome now blocks it
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page or ad script loads
can: Test whether your computer has certain programs listening, by timing quick requests
Check whether a companion desktop app is installed
Link web activity to an app on the same device
cannot: Do this silently in Chrome 142 and newer, which shows a pop up first
See files or data inside the programs it finds
Reach other devices on your network without the local network pop up
Work on iPhone browsers against apps, which are sandboxed from each other
limits.reach_label: Your own device, if not blocked
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge now ask first. Firefox and Safari still allow the quiet checks, though they only find what a site already expects. Android apps have been caught doing this.

story.what_it_is: A web page quietly checks which programs are running on your own computer or home network.
story.for_you: You never see it. A page you visit can try to connect to your own computer and learn which apps are open. The answer helps a site decide who you are.
story.for_makers: Some sites use it for fraud checks, such as spotting remote control software. Others have used it to collect hidden signals about the visitor. Browsers are adding rules to stop it.

use_cases.example: A bank site checks for common remote access tools on the visitor's machine. If one is running, it blocks the transfer to stop a scam call from taking over.
An ad script tests a list of local ports to build a hidden fingerprint of installed apps, which adds to a profile without cookies.
A browser game tries to connect to a helper app on a local port. If it answers, the game unlocks desktop features for that player.
A messaging web page checks a local port to see if the desktop app is running. If so, it opens chats there and not in the tab.
A developer tool in the browser connects to a helper on localhost to read files, so the site can show them in the page.
A fraud tool on a checkout page watches for debugging or automation tools open on the buyer's computer.
A company portal checks for its security agent on a local port before it lets staff sign in.

technical_bounds: Chrome 142 gates local requests behind a prompt
Firefox and Safari have no prompt yet (unverified at 2026-11)

value.abuse: Fraud detection by eBay, tracking ID bridging, router attacks

history.change: eBay port scanning reported by Nullsweep
Local Mess: Meta and Yandex localhost ID linking on Android disclosed
